subject: research/robofab-cell-monitor
professional: an operations-research / manufacturing-systems queueing researcher (the kind who referees for IISE Transactions or uses Buzacott and Shanthikumar's Stochastic Models of Manufacturing Systems), who also knows print-farm operations; checking first: whether the 'exact upper bound' is really an upper bound under the stochastic model the simulation runs, whether the simulation reproduces and agrees with an independent implementation, whether quoted gains are statistically resolved, and how the result sits against unreliable-machine / rework queueing literature and 3D-print failure-detection work

evidence.correctness: Ran it: `python3.13 experiments/run.py` on a scratch copy reproduces experiments/results.txt byte for byte in 10 s (numpy 2.5.3). Independent recomputations: (1) failure probabilities 1-exp(-0.3*20/60) = 0.0952 and 1-exp(-0.3) = 0.2592 match the README's 9.5% and 25.9%; (2) hand renewal-reward bound, blind, P=6: printer minutes per good part 0.5*(24/0.904837 + 64/0.740818) = 56.458 -> 6.376 parts/h, arm 60/(0.5*(4/0.9048+4/0.7408)) = 12.220 parts/h, matching 6.38 and 12.22; (3) closed form for a 10 min camera, printing minutes per attempt d + (1-e^{-lam(T-d)})/lam = 19.754 (A) and 54.24 (B) -> 6.866 parts/h at P=6 and 2.289 at P=2, matching 6.87 and 2.29; (4) an independent discrete-event simulation written by the auditor from the README's model description (scratchpad indep_sim.py, Python's random module, 200 seeds) gives 6.145 +/- 0.021 blind and 6.614 +/- 0.020 camera at P=6 (repo 6.13 +/- 0.05, 6.64 +/- 0.05), 6.06 vs 6.04 with 0.2 false stops/h, 12.115 vs 12.08 at P=16 blind, 2.300 vs 2.30 at P=2 camera; instant camera 6.89 +/- 0.02 vs 6.82 +/- 0.04 (1.6 SE, partial). (5) The headline arithmetic: 6.82/6.13 = +11.3%, interpolated false-stop break-even 0.1 + 0.1*(0.16/0.25) = 0.164, 4.39/6.13 = -28.4%, bound gaps 1.9/4.1/7.2/10.8/12.4% all recompute. One wrong claim found by recomputation: bound() evaluates attempt_stats at the mean print time (deterministic T) while every experiment runs lognormal cv 0.3; averaging the same closed form over lognormal T (Monte Carlo, 400k draws) gives 2.315 (P=2, camera) not 2.289, and the shipped simulation at 200 seeds gives 2.321 +/- 0.012, above the shipped 'upper bound' by 2.7 SE (delay 0: 2.400 +/- 0.011 vs 2.380). The simulated numbers are right; the 'exact upper bound' label is not.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: 8 tests pass (`PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed in 0.30 s); run.py regenerates results.txt identically; figure.py regenerates gain_vs_printers.svg identically (diffed); the four sweeps in the README all present in results.txt; the research page builds (`research/_homepage/build.py --out <scratch>` writes robofab-cell-monitor/index.html with the figure and the AI-assistance/stylised footer). No TODOs or stubs. Stale: README says run.py takes 'about 1 min'; it takes 10 s.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 1 caught, 4 SURVIVED: doubling the camera delay inside simulate (cell.py:135), dropping the 1/s retry factor from the arm load in bound (cell.py:70), dropping false stops from the success probability (cell.py:53), and dropping false stops from the sim's bad-print test (cell.py:134). Only inverting the good-print branch (cell.py:148) was caught. No test checks a false-stop result, the arm bound with failures, or any simulated camera rate against the bound; the closed-form tests cover attempt_stats only at delay 0 and delay 1e6.
evidence.craft: Read cell.py (178 lines), tests/test_cell.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py. A compact, readable event simulation, not a copy of an earlier engine, seeded and reproducible. Defects: attempt_stats integrates numerically (trapezoid, n=4000) what has a closed form d + (1-e^{-lam(T-d)})/lam (with false stops a similar closed form), and ignores cv though bound() is called with cv-bearing configs; `monitor_delay: float = None` mistyped; the walrus `q_print.append(j_ := jid)` and semicolon chains hurt readability; CellConfig default horizon 24 h while every run uses 48 h. Acceptable to a senior Python reviewer with those noted.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt: every bullet number matches (gains 10.2/6.7/8.4/7.7/6.2/4.5/0.8; delays 6.82..6.16; false stops 6.29/6.04/4.39; failure-rate gains 0.0..28.4; bound gaps 1.9..12.4). Not backed: README:13 'an upper bound that the simulation sits below by 0 to 12%' and 'exact per-attempt success and printing time' are false for the cv 0.3 runs (the camera sim at P=2 is 2.30 against a 2.29 'bound' in results.txt itself, and 2.321 +/- 0.012 at 200 seeds); README:13 says the bound 'overstates the gain at 12 printers (it says 0%, the simulation +4.5%)', which is an understatement, not an overstatement; README:20 'about 1 min' is 10 s. Limits and the illustrative-parameters statement are clear and honest; the built page carries the AI-assistance and stylised-results footer; 'No external result is cited or reproduced' is stated openly.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it, and one did: research/robofab-cell-detector reuses its cell, parameters and failure model. But the headline 'helps most when the printers set the limit, gain disappears once the arm does' is the standard bottleneck consequence (a camera saves printer time, not arm time) that the analytic bound already gives as a 7.7% printer-limited gain at every P; the simulated per-P gains (10.2, 6.7, 8.4, 7.7, 6.2) are reported to a tenth of a percent with no standard error on the difference (about 2% at P=2 from the two 0.03 SEs on 2.1), so the apparent peak at P=2 is noise. No common random numbers between blind and camera runs. Nearest prior work not cited: unreliable-machine and rework models with preemptive-repeat-different failures (Gaver 1962; Buzacott and Shanthikumar 1993, the same book robofab-cell-fesc cites), and print-failure detection (Obico/The Spaghetti Detective; Petsiuk and Pearce 2020 open-source CV failure detection for FFF). Sound as a stylised exercise; not new.
evidence.domain: Against the queueing practice for such cells: the bound is the right renewal-reward utilisation bound (attempts are i.i.d., cost per good part = E[cost per attempt]/P(success), recomputed by hand) but evaluates the success probability at the mean print time, so by Jensen it is not an upper bound when print times vary; a referee would ask for the bound to average over the print-time distribution (or to be called a deterministic-time approximation). The failure model (Poisson hazard during printing, total loss, fixed delay, Poisson false stops) is stated with its limits. Missing what a referee checks: paired comparisons or SE of the gain, prior-work positioning, and any sourced failure rate (none; all illustrative, stated).

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible stylised study: results.txt and the figure regenerate byte for byte in 10 s, the hand renewal-reward bounds (6.376, 12.220, 6.866 parts/h) match, and an independent simulation written from the README's model agrees with the repo's within noise at five of six configurations. It does not meet the bar. Verification is weak (4 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including the camera delay and both false-stop paths), and the one analytic claim is wrong as stated: the 'exact upper bound' ignores the cv 0.3 print-time variability the experiments use, and the shipped simulation beats it at 2 printers with a camera (2.321 +/- 0.012 against 2.289). The README also says the bound 'overstates' a gain it understates. The research contribution is the textbook bottleneck consequence with no prior work cited and no standard error on the quoted gains. Fix the bound (average over lognormal T, or relabel it a deterministic-time approximation), add tests that pin the camera and false-stop paths, and position against unreliable-machine queueing and print-failure-detection work.
